title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Emma Clarke
summary: Operating playbook and canonical templates for Developer Experience docs: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues with canonical fixes.
body:
Overview:

This document defines the standard templates, operating procedures, and canonical support fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues we track with their canonical fixes. The goal is to ensure consistent, high-quality, reviewer-approved content that reduces time-to-onboard for external developers and minimizes repeat support tickets.

Scope:

- SDK guides (JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and one-page templates for common flows (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming)
- API examples and runnable snippets (curl, HTTP, SDK code)
- Docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle, CI, publishing, rollback)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes maintained by DevEx + Support

Ownership and SLAs:

- Content owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) team (primary)
- Reviewer pool: SDK engineers + Product SDK owners (secondary)
- Publishing SLA: new quickstart -> published within 5 business days after PR merge; major SDK guide update -> published within 10 business days.
- Support feedback loop: any support issue reported more than 3 times in a 30-day window must result in a docs action (update or new quickstart) within 7 business days.

Templates and Required Sections:

1) SDK Guide template (recommended filename: sdk-<lang>-guide-YYYY.json)

- Title
- Short description (1-2 sentences)
- Prerequisites (SDK version, runtime, API key scope)
- Installation (copy-paste commands)
- Authentication example
- Basic usage (hello-world sample)
- Key features (streaming, function calling, batching, caching) with examples
- Error handling & retry guidance (status codes, transient vs permanent)
- Performance tips (connection pooling, request concurrency)
- Test / local debug tips (mocking the API)
- Links: API reference, quickstarts, CHANGELOG, release notes

2) Quickstart template (filename: quickstart-<flow>-YYYY.json)

- Title and TL;DR (2-line)
- Use case & expected outcome
- Prerequisites (account, credits, region)
- Step-by-step with numbered commands and code snippets
- Expected output and verification steps
- Troubleshooting section with common errors
- Next steps and recommended follow-ups (e.g., move to SDK guide, prod checklist)

3) API Example template (filename: api-example-<topic>-YYYY.json)

- Short description and status (verified / unverified)
- curl example (full request + expected response snippet)
- SDK example for each supported language (compact, copy-paste ready)
- Streaming example (if applicable)
- Notes on permissions, headers, content types, and throttling

Example: Minimal text generation quickstart (snippet)

1. Prerequisites
- API key with "generate" scope
- Node 18+ or Python 3.10+

2. curl example

curl -X POST \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-1.0", "input": "Write a friendly welcome message for a new user."}'

3. JavaScript (Node) snippet

const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Write a friendly welcome message for a new user.' });
console.log(resp.output);

Docs Site Operating Procedures (content lifecycle):

- Authoring
  1. Create a new file from the matching template in the quickstarts-and-templates folder.
  2. Add metadata fields (title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated, reviewers, labels).
  3. Ensure the doc follows the required sections for the chosen template.

- Review
  1. Open a PR against the docs repo (branch: docs/<short-title>).
  2. Assign 2 reviewers from the reviewer pool and at least one SDK owner for code snippets.
  3. CI checks: spell-check, linter (style rules), runnable-snippet test (curl and SDK smoke test).
  4. Address review comments within 3 business days.

- Publishing
  1. Merge PR; CI will trigger the docs-site build and preview deployment.
  2. Validate the preview for broken links and snippet rendering.
  3. Promote to production. If a regression is found post-publish, follow the rollback procedure.

- Rollback procedure
  1. Revert the change via a new PR referencing the incident.
  2. Notify #devex-docs and #support with impact, rollback commit, and timeline.
  3. Create a post-rollback follow-up to correct the root cause and re-publish.

Runnable Snippets and CI Testing:

- Every API example and quickstart that includes code must have a runnable curl test as part of docs CI. For SDK code, include a small smoke test that runs under an integration flag (DOCS_SMOKE=true) using a short request.
- Secrets: CI must use ephemeral test keys with limited scopes and rate limits; never store long-lived keys in the repo.

Support Playbook: Top support issues and canonical fixes

Priority: Issues are ranked by frequency and severity. The list below is canonical and must be referenced in support triage and new-hire training. Each entry includes: symptom, immediate workaround, root cause, permanent fix, owner.

1) "401 / invalid_api_key" on first SDK request
- Symptom: SDK returns 401 with response code invalid_api_key.
- Workaround: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY env var set, re-run with --auth header.
- Root cause: Commonly using personal key created on sandbox or expired key.
- Permanent fix: Add explicit note in quickstarts to use "Account > API keys > Create key (docs-scope)" and include example token permissions.
- Owner: DevEx + Auth team

2) Streaming responses hang or stop mid-stream
- Symptom: Long-running streaming sessions freeze after ~30s or deliver partial tokens.
- Workaround: Use non-streaming fallback or retry with exponential backoff.
- Root cause: Ingress proxy (nginx) idle timeouts or client TCP connection resets.
- Permanent fix: Docs update to include recommended client keepalive headers and platform config; infra fix to increase idle_timeout to 120s for streaming routes.
- Owner: Eng Platform + DevEx

3) High latency during peak traffic for small requests
- Symptom: 95th percentile tail latency spikes for short prompt workloads.
- Workaround: Use batching and prefer dedicated endpoints; add client-side retry for 503 transient errors.
- Root cause: Autoscaling policy and cold-starts on dedicated pools; suboptimal request sizes causing scheduling overhead.
- Permanent fix: Add quickstart section on batching configuration and include SDK helper functions; infra tuning as per Performance Standards doc.
- Owner: Serving Runtime + DevEx

4) Mismatched response schema for function/tool calling examples
- Symptom: Example shows JSON schema but SDK returns nested objects or a string-encoded JSON.
- Workaround: Parse string JSON with JSON.parse as needed; add validation in user code.
- Root cause: Version skew between example and SDK (older SDK auto-stringifies responses).
- Permanent fix: Keep API example status field explicit (verified/required SDK version) and add automated snippet tests that verify schema shape.
- Owner: SDK owners + DevEx

Change log and metrics to monitor:

- Maintain a CHANGELOG entry for each published quickstart or SDK guide update.
- Dashboards to monitor: docs-snippet-failure-rate, docs-ci-flaky-tests, support-tickets-by-doc-page (tracked in customer-success).

Appendix: Checklist for authors (copy into PR description)

- [ ] Title follows naming guidelines and contains year (e.g., quickstart-text-generation-2026)
- [ ] Metadata fields filled and status set appropriately
- [ ] Code snippets are copy-paste runnable and include language tags
- [ ] CI smoke tests exist for curl and SDK snippets
- [ ] At least 2 reviewers assigned and comments addressed
- [ ] Labels added (max 8) and related_pages linked
- [ ] Support playbook entry created/updated if doc resolves a recurring ticket

If you have questions or need a template branch created, ping #devex-docs or open a ticket in the DevEx backlog (project: DE-Docs).
